description.text: We are an integrated electric utility company engaged in the transmission and distribution of substantially all of the electricity in Korea. Through our six wholly-owned generation subsidiaries, we also generate the substantial majority of electricity produced in Korea. As of December 31, 2025, we and our generation subsidiaries owned approximately 53.4% of the total electricity generation capacity in Korea (excluding plants generating electricity primarily for private or emergency use). In 2025, we sold to our customers 549,417 gigawatt-hours of electricity. We purchase electricity principally from our generation subsidiaries and, to a lesser extent, from independent power producers. Of the 545,192 gigawatt-hours of electricity we purchased in 2025, 33.2% was generated by KHNP, our wholly-owned nuclear and hydroelectric power generation subsidiary, 32.7% was generated by our wholly-owned five non-nuclear generation subsidiaries and 34.1% was generated by independent power producers that trade electricity to us through the cost-based pool system of power trading (excluding independent power producers that supply electricity under power purchase agreements with us). Our five non-nuclear generation subsidiaries are KOSEP, KOMIPO, KOWEPO, KOSPO and EWP, each of which is wholly owned by us and is incorporated in Korea. We derive substantially all of our revenues and profit from Korea, and substantially all of our assets are located in Korea.

about.description_short: Korea Electric Power Corp is an electric utility company in which the government of South Korea holds a controlling stake. The firm operates in the following segments: Transmission and distribution, Electric power generation, Electric power generation, Plant maintenance & engineering service, and Others. Most of the energy produced by the company comes from its nuclear and coal-fired assets. Korea Electric Power generates revenue primarily through the Transmission and distribution segment.

analysis_md:
# KEP — Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO)
v5 run, 2026-10-17 (engine release 5.4.0). In scope (price $10.63 per ADS, nasdaq_quote_api; engine market_cap_est $6,824,078,138.51).

All engine figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed. FY2025 filing figures and post-FY2024 prints are from the cited 20-F / search results, as noted, and are labelled as outside the engine history where they are.

## What it is
South Korea's state-controlled electric utility: the sole nationwide transmission and distribution operator, buying and generating power through its generation subsidiaries (including KHNP for nuclear) and selling to effectively every household, business and factory in the country under government-set tariffs. Listed on the Korea Exchange (common stock) and on NYSE as ADSs — one ADS represents one-half of one common share (FY2025 20-F cover and Item 9.A). The Korean government and Korea Development Bank are the controlling holders, and KEPCO doubles as a price-stabilization policy tool — that dual role, not competition, is what drives its economics.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2024 (latest year in the engine history; 20-F via EDGAR companyfacts, FX-converted from KRW at period-end ECB rates, from financials_history.csv):** revenue $62,953,220,200; net income $2,462,938,240; operating cash flow $10,795,758,880; capex $9,666,905,160 (tag: PurchaseOfPropertyPlantAndEquipmentClassifiedAsInvestingActivities); SBC $0 — by filing override, see OVERRIDE; D&A $9,518,201,400.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2024: $1,128,853,720 total = $0.88/ADS** (dcf_numbers.json: base_oe_total_latest_fy $1,128,853,720; base_oe_latest_per_share $0.8792187603980215, per ADS after the 0.5 ratio scaling).
- Maintenance version FY2024: $1,128,853,720 (financials_history.csv, oe_maintenance) — identical to the conservative figure in FY2024.
- **OE positive in only 2 of the last 5 fiscal years** (dcf_numbers.json: oe_positive_years_of_last_5 "2/5"). The crisis years dominate the history: conservative OE was -$28,301,258,620 in FY2022 and -$9,537,382,470 in FY2023 (financials_history.csv totals) after tariffs were frozen through the post-invasion fuel spike while power-purchase and fuel costs exploded.
- **Base used = the engine's normalized base (median of last 3 FY OE/share): -$7.43/ADS** (dcf_numbers.json: base_oe_per_share / base_oe_normalized_per_share -7.428283615626673, source median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). The median year of the window is FY2023, a crisis year — the base is genuinely distorted, and that distortion is investigated under STALE_FY / the verdict below rather than corrected by hand: no code-computed newer base exists for this IFRS filer, and even the best single engine year (FY2024, +$0.88/ADS) sits against net debt of $12,427,953,360 (dcf_numbers.json; basis LongtermBorrowings + CurrentBorrowingsAndCurrentPortionOfNoncurrentBorrowings) plus lease liabilities of $2,515,630,080, so no defensible base in the engine outputs supports a positive DCF at a $10.63 ADS price.
- Share count is flat: 641,964,077 diluted shares, share_cagr 0.0 (dcf_numbers.json) — a decade with no dilution and no buyback.

## OVERRIDE — SBC $0 (filing) and ADS ratio 0.5 (filing)
- **The gap:** the preliminary engine run exited 4 with `DATA_GAP:sbc` — SBC missing for fiscal years 2022, 2023, 2024 of the last 3 under every tag the engine reads, and a separate `ADS_RATIO_MISSING` flag for this 20-F filer. No tier was emitted, correctly.
- **SBC decision (bounded authority (a), kind "filing"):** judgment.json carries `sbc_override = {value: 0, kind: "filing"}`. KEPCO has no equity-settled share-based payment expense to subtract: the FY2025 Form 20-F (filed 2026-04-29, accession 0001193125-26-190113), Item 16G NYSE-standards comparison, states "We currently do not have any equity compensation plans"; the term "share-based" appears nowhere in the 20-F; and EDGAR companyfacts carries no SBC fact for this filer in any year under any candidate tag. Same treatment as SQM, TS and LTM in this sweep. The override carries an ack_reason: it is out-of-band by construction because the engine's last filed SBC value is null (dcf_numbers.json override_checks: last_filed_value null, out_of_band true, ack_reason_present true).
- **Measured impact (dcf_numbers.json override_impact):** none on the numbers — base_oe_per_share_zero_fill -7.428283615626673 → base_oe_per_share_final -7.428283615626673, weighted IRR null both ways. Its effect is binary: without it there is no tier at all. The override filled every history period 2015-2024 (overrides_applied periods_filled), and an override never replaces a filed value — there simply are no filed SBC values.
- **ADS decision (bounded authority (d)):** judgment.json carries `ads_ratio = {ratio: 0.5}` from the filer's own 20-F (cover: "American depositary shares, each representing one-half of share of common stock"; Item 9.A: "One ADS represents one-half of one share of our common stock"). Per-share figures are scaled x0.5 so they are comparable to the $10.63 ADS price (flag ADS_RATIO_APPLIED).

## Moat: 4/10 — durable national franchise, confiscated economics
Justification: Exclusive national T&D franchise with captive essential-service demand and generation scale, but the regulator/government — also the controlling holder — sets tariffs politically and froze them through the 2021-2023 fuel spike, so the franchise has no pricing power and its measured ROIC through the cycle is deeply negative (roic_proxy -47.01% in 2022, -6.36% in 2023, 9.78% in 2024). A durable monopoly whose economics are capped and periodically confiscated is a weak moat, not a wide one.

## Final verdict
**Tier F (no_cash_generation).** The normalized conservative OE base is −$7.43/ADS because the median window (FY2022–24) carries the tariff-freeze crisis years — OE positive in only 2 of the last 5 years — so no IV@15% or hurdle-clearing price is computable at $10.63 on this method. Underneath the window, FY2024 printed +$0.88/ADS and the filed FY2025 shows a profitable utility recovering; that recovery is real but is not a positive *normalized* OE stream, and even the best single year cannot carry $12.43B of net debt to a hurdle-clearing DCF at this price.
